references.text: Isaiah 9:1-2 predicts that the people walking in darkness will see a great light, a direct counterpart to Jesus' warning that those who walk in darkness do not know where they are going.
Isaiah 42:6-7 describes the Messiah as a light for the nations to open the eyes of those sitting in darkness, reflecting Jesus' identity as the light in John 12:35.
In John 8:12, Jesus declares that he is the light of the world and that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, a direct theological extension of the warning in 12:35.
John 11:9-10 uses the same imagery regarding the light of day and the darkness that overtakes people, linking it to walking in the light so as not to stumble.
John 1:4-5 establishes that the light shines in the darkness and the darkness has not overcome it, providing context for Jesus' claim that the light is still present.
1 Peter 2:9 describes believers as called out of darkness into his wonderful light, a direct response to the call to walk as children of the light.
Ephesians 5:8-11 urges Christians to walk as children of the light and exposes the deeds done in darkness, an ethical application of Jesus' words in John 12:35.
